title: Private deployments: VPC & On-Prem deployment, day-2 ops, upgrade/rollback, customer requirements library
author: Aria Chen
body:
Overview

This document is a comprehensive reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates deployment guides, reference architectures, on-prem packaging details, day-2 operations, and upgrade/rollback procedures, and provides a customer requirements library for common enterprise requests. Intended audience: platform engineers, site reliability engineers, solutions engineers, and customer technical contacts.

Scope

- VPC-hosted private control-plane deployments (customer VPC with Redwood-managed control plane endpoints)
- Fully on-prem (air-gapped) installations using Redwood on-prem packaging
- Day-2 operational runbooks: monitoring, scaling, backups, maintenance windows
- Upgrade and rollback procedures with canary and staged rollouts
- Customer requirements matrix covering networking, compliance, and operational expectations

Key goals

1. Provide repeatable, secure, testable deployment steps.
2. Minimize downtime for upgrades and configuration changes.
3. Capture common customer constraints and pre-approved patterns.

Before you start (high-level prerequisites)

| Area | Minimum requirement | Notes |
|------|---------------------|-------|
| Account & Billing | Active Redwood contract and entitlement for Private product | Legal + Sales must confirm entitlements. |
| Network | VPC subnets (private), NAT/egress, peering/VPN/BGW set up | See Network section below. |
| Identity & Auth | Customer KMS, OIDC provider, and SAML for SSO (optional) | KMS for model keys and audit. |
| Hardware (on-prem) | N nodes: minimum 3 control-plane + GPU nodes per sizing guide | See sizing. |
| Ops access | Customer point-of-contact and SSH/Jumphost | Account team must provide contacts. |

Reference architecture (two canonical patterns)

1) VPC private control plane with customer data-plane (recommended for most enterprise customers)

- Control plane endpoints (management plane) run in Redwood-managed cloud region using mutual TLS.
- Customer data-plane (inference workers, stateful services) run inside customer VPC / cloud account.
- Network peering or private link + IP allowlists for control plane communication.
- KMS integration via cross-account IAM roles or KMS proxy.

2) Fully on-prem (air-gapped)

- All components run in customer datacenter or private cloud.
- Packaging delivered as signed OCI images and Helm charts (airgap bundle includes tar.gz of images and chart).
- Optional hardware HSM/KMS for key custody.

Diagram (textual)

- VPC: Customer VPC -> Private subnets for inference nodes -> NAT / Proxy -> Redwood control plane (mTLS link)
- Onprem: Jump host -> internal Kubernetes cluster -> GPU nodes -> Local KMS/HSM -> Optional isolated storage NFS / S3-compatible gateway

Sizing guidance (example)

| Workload | gGPU type | Initial cluster size (workers) | Notes |
|---------|----------|-----------------------------:|-------|
| Small real-time LLM, <50 qps | A100 40GB or H100 | 2-4 GPU nodes | Use quantized models for cost efficiency. |
| Medium throughput, caching | H100 80GB | 4-8 GPU nodes | Enable KV-cache and batching. |
| High throughput, multi-tenant | M60/NVIDIA equivalent | 8+ nodes + autoscaling | Use dedicated pools per tenant. |

Network & security requirements

- IP allowlist for control plane: provide static IP ranges.
- Outbound access: control plane requires egress to Redwood control-plane endpoints on ports 443 and 5222 (for agent heartbeat) - confirm firewall rules.
- PrivateLink/DirectConnect: optional for reduced latency.
- KMS: customer must provide KMS endpoint and a service principal with encrypt/decrypt permissions.
- TLS: mTLS required between data-plane agents and Redwood control plane; TLS certs are auto-provisioned via signed CSR or can use customer-provided certs for on-prem.

On-prem packaging and delivery artifacts

- Delivered artifacts (airgapped):
  - OCI image tarball (signed) for runtime components
  - Helm chart bundle: redwood-inference-chart-vX.Y.Z.tgz
  - Installer CLI: redwood-install-cli-vX.Y.Z (Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 where applicable)
  - SHA256 checksums and GPG signatures
  - Documentation bundle with manifests, default values, and manifests for optional add-ons (prometheus, loki, fluentd)

- Installation options:
  - Helm chart installation for clusters with internet access.
  - Offline installer (tar + CLI) for air-gapped clusters.

Deployment procedure: VPC (recommended)

1. Pre-deployment checklist
   - Confirm entitlements and subscription (account team).
   - Confirm VPC subnets, route tables, and NAT config.
   - Customer KMS endpoint and IAM role prepared.
   - Provide Redwood with allowlisted CIDRs for control plane.

2. Provision infrastructure
   - Create EKS/GKE/AKS cluster as per platform standard or use existing cluster with required capacity.
   - Create dedicated namespaces: redwood-system, redwood-inference.
   - Install CNI and other baseline operators (CSI, metrics-server).

3. Install Redwood control-plane agent in customer VPC
   - Configure redwood-agent values.yaml:

```yaml
agent:
  controlPlaneEndpoint: "control.redwood.example:443"
  mtls: enabled
  kms: 
    provider: customer-kms
    endpoint: "kms.customer.example"
```

   - Helm install: helm upgrade --install redwood-agent ./redwood-agent-chart -f values.yaml

4. Smoke tests
   - Validate mTLS handshake: redwood-agent logs show successful registration.
   - Run a sample inference job: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://<agent-ip>/v1/generate

5. Promote to production
   - Apply RBAC rules, SLO monitoring dashboards, and role separation.

On-prem deployment procedure (air-gapped)

1. Deliver airgap bundle and verify signatures.
2. Transfer artifacts to internal registry and import OCI images.
3. Run redwood-install-cli install --bundle ./redwood-airgap-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz --namespace redwood-system
4. Post-install validation: container images start, CRDs registered, components show Ready.

Day-2 operations (runbook highlights)

Monitoring & observability
- Required: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), Loki/ELK for logs, Jaeger/Zipkin for traces.
- Out-of-the-box dashboards: token-level cost, per-model latency p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rate.
- Default alert thresholds:
  - Control plane heartbeat missing > 2 minutes -> Pager (sev2)
  - p99 latency > 2s for 1 minute -> Pager (sev1)
  - GPU memory pressure > 90% for 2 minutes -> Alert to on-call

Scaling and capacity management
- Autoscaling: node autoscaler for non-GPU nodes, custom scaling policies for GPU pools.
- Batching adjustments: use Redwood Optimize recommendations to tune batch sizes and max latency budgets.

Backups & disaster recovery
- Config backup cadence: etcd/config maps: daily snapshots stored to customer S3-compatible bucket.
- Model artifacts: store immutable model artifacts in versioned object storage with lifecycle rules.
- Restore test: perform quarterly restore drills in a staging environment.

Maintenance windows and patching
- Maintenance windows: weekly 02:00-05:00 local time recommended.
- Kernel/driver updates on GPU nodes: one node at a time, drain, upgrade, validate, uncordon.

Upgrade and rollback procedure (recommended practice)

Principles
- Blue/green or canary rollouts for control-plane and data-plane components.
- Preflight checks: unit tests, integration smoke tests, performance regression checks using standard eval harness.

Procedure (control plane patch)
1. Create release branch and build artifact.
2. Deploy to staging cluster, run full E2E + perf suite (target: no >5% regression on p95 latency).
3. Canary deploy to 5% of nodes in production data-plane (label subset).
4. Monitor key metrics for 30-60 minutes: errors, latency, KV-cache hit rate, GPU utilization.
5. If metrics stable, increase to 25% and repeat.
6. Full rollout via Helm with chart version locking.
7. If regression detected: trigger rollback via helm rollback to previous release and run rollback verification checklist.

Rollback checklist
- Confirm rollback target version and manifest SHA.
- Notify stakeholders and pause any automated CI pipelines.
- helm rollback <release> <revision> --wait --timeout 15m
- Validate system health and run smoke tests against production traffic shadow.
- If rollback fails: escalate to Redwood SRE on-call and open incident with logs and heap dumps.

Customer requirements library (common asks and prescriptive answers)

| Customer ask | Typical requirement | Redwood guidance / accepted pattern |
|--------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Air-gapped install | No outbound connectivity | Use airgap bundle, import images to private registry, map KMS to HSM gateway |
| FIPS-compliant crypto | FIPS validated modules required | Use customer-provided FIPS KMS and enable FIPS build (supported on request) |
| On-board to corporate SSO | SAML/Okta | Configure SAML connector; provide metadata XML to Redwood |
| Data residency | Models and embeddings must not leave region | Deploy data-plane in customer region; use regional object storage |
| Audit logging | 365-day retention | Enable audit-log-forwarding to central syslog/S3; configure retention lifecycle |

Appendices

Appendix A - Example values.yaml snippets

```yaml
redwood:
  agent:
    controlPlaneEndpoint: "control.redwood.example:443"
    mtls: true
    logLevel: info
  modelStore:
    s3Endpoint: "s3.customer.example"
    bucket: "redwood-models-prod"
```

Appendix B - Troubleshooting quick hits

- Agent fails to register: check DNS resolution to control plane, validate TLS certificate chain, verify outbound firewall rules.
- High p99 latency: inspect KV-cache hit rate and batch size config; consider increasing batch window or adding GPUs.
- Failed upgrade: check helm history and check CRD compatibility changes.
